{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.",
    "When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model persists in upward trend — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day until reversion stabilizes.",
    "If sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or 0.20), model may be overconfident — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is >90.5 and true outcome drops below 85, apply downward correction of 2–4% for next 5 days unless sentiment turns positive.",
    "If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows volatility (e.g., ±5% swings), reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day to match sentiment-driven noise.",
    "When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and model is flat, model underestimates — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days to align with sentiment momentum."
  ]
}
